I've been working this land for 15 years now. I know Quzhou's soil — it's heavy clay-loam, alkaline, and the groundwater table is deep enough that I can't slack on irrigation timing. My sons help when they're back from the city, but mostly it's me and my wife. At my age, I don't chase new things. I stick with what my land rewards.

My wheat-maize rotation is the backbone of everything — 12 mu for that. I'll leave 3 mu for cotton and 3 mu for chili. Cotton prices have been rough, but I know how to grow it and it gives me something to do in the hot months. Chili I sell at the local market; my wife handles most of that.

For wheat, I'll plant Jimai 22 — it's proven here and my neighbor swears by it. I put down basal fertilizer at sowing, then top-dress at jointing. Four irrigations: sowing water, winter water, jointing, and grain fill. I spray twice — once for weeds in winter, once for aphids and rust in spring. Rotary tillage before sowing, same as always.

After wheat harvest in June, I go straight into maize — Zhengdan 958 hybrid, same as last year. I won't waste time. Two irrigations, maybe three if July is dry. Two pesticide passes for corn borer and fall armyworm.

Cotton goes in the remaining 3 mu. I keep nitrogen moderate — too much and it bolls poorly. Six pesticide applications minimum because of bollworm. Three irrigations timed to flowering and boll setting.

Chili I plant from seedlings I raise myself in March. It needs the most water of everything I grow — six irrigations through the season. I apply pesticides four times for aphids and blight.
